collection.description: A child asks why a soft toy needs ears when it cannot hear.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (child) asks why a soft toy needs ears when it cannot hear.

a1.name: Outcome A1
a1.text: (adult), a weaver, says the ears help the toy resemble an animal.

a2.name: Outcome A2
a2.text: (child) notices that ears also make the toy easy to recognize.

b1.name: Outcome B1
b1.text: (adult) says the toy listens to secrets, then clarifies it is make-believe.

b2.name: Outcome B2
b2.text: (child) invents an amusing tale about a toy hearing the ocean.

c1.name: Outcome C1
c1.text: (child) says the ears make the toy look friendly.

c2.name: Outcome C2
c2.text: (child) designs a toy with unusually long ears.

d1.name: Outcome D1
d1.text: (adult), a naturalist, explains that ears help many animals hear.

d2.name: Outcome D2
d2.text: (child) notices that different animals have very different ears.
